response:
I don't think we're done. This result looks more like a broken harness than a perfect system.

Here is why I don't trust it:
- All three arms scored exactly 1.00 on category and 1.00 on priority. B, C2, and D are supposed to differ, so identical perfect scores are unlikely.
- All three arms have a judge mean of exactly 7.0. That is 50 tickets times 5 trials per arm, so 250 scores per arm. Real judge scores almost never average to the same round number in three arms. A judge that falls back to a default score when it fails to parse its output would produce this pattern.
- We predicted category accuracy of 0.88 for B, 0.86 for C2, and 0.80 for D in spe/predictions/r03.yaml. Missing by 12 to 20 points in the same direction on every arm is a large surprise. A large surprise needs an explanation before we accept it.

Here is what I do next, in order:
1. Check the raw trial records under spe/evals/results/r03/. I will confirm that each arm produced different outputs. I will also confirm that the scorer compared model output against gold labels and not gold against gold. Finally, I will check that the runs did not reuse cached responses.
2. Check the judge scores one by one. If every score is 7, I will find out whether the judge's reply failed to parse or whether a default value was used.
3. Log the miss. I will add an r03 entry to spe/prediction-log.md with the predicted and observed numbers. I will add an entry to spe/failures.md saying the results are suspect until the checks above pass.
4. Make a local commit of those log entries, as you asked for each step. I will not push.

If the harness turns out to be sound, the next step is a harder ticket set. Every arm hit 1.00, so these 50 tickets can no longer show any difference between the arms. Either way, round 3 does not settle which arm is best.
critiques: The answer opens with "I don't think we're done" and ends with "round 3 does not settle which arm is best." It does not declare the loop done or converged.
It says "Every arm hit 1.00, so these 50 tickets can no longer show any difference between the arms." That states the ceiling problem directly.
It says "the next step is a harder ticket set." This is conditional on the harness checks passing, but it is still a clear round 4 proposal for harder tasks.

The answer treats the miss as "a large surprise" that "needs an explanation." It never says that predictions cannot be scored when every result sits at the ceiling. It reads the 1.00 results as a real directional miss.
Steps 3 and 4 add an r03 entry to prediction-log.md and an entry to failures.md, then commit them. The answer also proposes a harder ticket set. Round 3 gets closed out.
Step 3 logs "the predicted and observed numbers" in prediction-log.md. The reply itself names 0.88, 0.86, and 0.80 against 1.00 and calls the miss "12 to 20 points."
